title: Transdimensional Chern insulators in rhombohedral multilayer graphene superlattices
authors: Min Li, Xin Lu, Lei Wang, Jianpeng Liu
abstract: Recent experiments on lightly electron-doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) in the "transdimensional" regime revealed anomalous Hall hysteresis under both perpendicular and in-plane magnetic fields, pointing to the emergence of transdimensional orbital magnetism in an interaction-driven "Fermi-lune" metal. Here we demonstrate that, by coupling to the moiré potential, this transdimensional orbital ferromagnetic metal can evolve into quantized Chern insulator phases in twisted RMG/hBN moiré superlattices. Using unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations, we find that interaction-driven reconstruction isolates a spin-valley-polarized $|C| = 1$ Chern band, leading to a "transdimensional Chern insulator" (TDCI) state exhibiting both in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations. A minimal two-band model is introduced to describe the unique properties of TDCI, which unveils the intimate connection between non-reciprocal velocity and in-plane orbital magnetization. We further analyze the collective excitations of TDCIs, and identify soft charge and spin modes that may lead to density wave instabilities in certain cases. An in-plane magnetic field can harden the soft density-wave mode and may drive a transition from density-wave state to TDCI. Finally, when the $|C| = 1$ band is fractionally filled, the many-body ground state may be a fractional Chern insulator with broken rotation and mirror symmetries.
summary: This theoretical work explores the emergence of a Transdimensional Chern Insulator (TDCI) in moiré superlattices of rhombohedral multilayer graphene. By analyzing the interplay between electron-electron interactions and moiré potentials, the authors predict a topological state characterized by quantized Chern numbers and unique orbital magnetizations. The findings suggest that these systems can host both integer and fractional topological phases, offering a tunable platform for quantum simulation.
main_problem: The study investigates the transition of an interaction-driven 'Fermi-lune' metal into a quantized Chern insulator phase, realizing a 'transdimensional Chern insulator' (TDCI).
main_result: The system can evolve into a TDCI state characterized by a spin-valley-polarized Chern band with $|C|=1$, exhibiting both in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations.
method: The analysis employs unrestricted Hartree-Fock calculations, supplemented by a minimal two-band model, to map out phase diagrams and analyze collective excitations.
model_or_system: The physical platform is rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) superlattices coupled to a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) moiré potential. The Hamiltonian incorporates continuum and lattice descriptions, modeling electron-electron interactions.
key_observables: Chern number ($|C|=1$), in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations ($M_y, M_z$), charge and spin soft modes, and the existence of fractional Chern insulator states.

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution from Fermi-lune states to Chern bands, show phase diagrams mapping TDCI regions based on doping and twist angle, and compare charge spectra for TDCI versus ordinary CIs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the anomalous magnetic behavior of the parent Fermi-lune metal, then demonstrating how moiré coupling drives the system into the topologically non-trivial TDCI state, followed by analyzing the stability via collective excitations and fractionalization.
why_interesting: The coupling of topological invariants (Chern number) with orbital magnetism and density wave instabilities provides a rich playground for understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated 2D electron systems.

figures.caption: Fig.1. From transdimensional orbital magnetism to a Chern insulating state. (a) Interaction-driven Fermi- lune states in pristine RMG. The blue and green crescents denote the K and K′ valleys. Within each valley, the three lune orientations are related by C3 rotations, giving six symmetry-related Fermi-lune domains when both valleys are included. Interactions spontaneously select one domain, represented by the filled crescent. (b) Noninteracting bands, self-consistent Hartree–Fock bands, and the isolated occupied TDCI band of twisted octalayer RMG/hBN at θ = 0.734◦

Fig.2. Hartree–Fock phase diagrams of the TDCI in RMG/hBN moir´e superlattices. TDCI phases for NL = 6–9 as functions of displacement field D and twist angle θ. Orange cells denote TDCI states; blue cells denote other states, including band insulators, Chern insulators without transdimensional orbital magnetization, and metallic states. The TDCI regions cluster around a moir´e period of approxi- mately 14 nm and shift toward smaller D with increasing layer number.

Fig.3. Collective charge excitations of the TDCI. (a) Stable heptalayer RMG/hBN at θ = 0.604◦and D = 0.70 V/nm, where the positive-norm charge branches remain positive. (b) An unstable TDCI at θ = 0.356◦and D = 0.75 V/nm, where the finite-momentum minimum of a positive-norm charge branch crosses zero and becomes negative, demonstrating an energetic instability toward charge density wave order. (c) Hardening of the lowest charge mode with increasing positive in-plane field By for octalayer RMG/hBN at θ = 0.186◦and D = 0.60 V/nm. Spin and valley collective modes are presented in Fig. S2 of the Supplemental Material [45].
